description:
Greetings,

We are college students seeking knowledge and development through experience. Our goal for this challenge is to build a public-friendly web tool that visualizes near-infrared time-lapse imagery to easily identify moving cosmic objects. We are seeking passionate team members with experience in UI/UX design, basic python skills, or astronomy API integration to help elevate our platform. we also welcome anyone with no prior experience who is eager to learn, contribute, and collaborate.
summary:
Ethereal Cosmos is an interactive web tool that shows where stars and objects are in the sky and how they move over time. We built a data pipeline that pulls SPHEREx, WISE and Gaia images from NASA’s IRSA archive, aligns frames taken on different dates, and detects moving objects such as the brown dwarf WISE 0855. Users explore everything on a clean Aladin sky map, step through time, and overlay Gaia and WISE data. A forecasting mode with a time slider predicts a star’s position and shows its past trajectory, age and expected lifetime. A dashboard adds a radar for possible icy objects, a top stars list and spectrum analysis, and accounts let users save and share their stars and views.

This answers the challenge by turning SPHEREx data into a readable map with a timeline of shifting star positions. It matters because space data is usually heavy and confusing; our light, fast and plain-language design lets students, researchers and curious people explore it easily.
details:
What it does and how it works
Ethereal Cosmos is an interactive web tool that shows where stars and objects are in the sky and how they move over time. A Python pipeline queries NASA’s IRSA archive for SPHEREx, WISE and Gaia data at a target’s coordinates, aligns images taken on different dates onto the same sky grid, and compares them to find moving objects such as the brown dwarf WISE 0855. A forecasting mode with a time slider predicts a star’s position and shows its past trajectory, age and expected lifetime. The results appear on an Aladin sky map, with a dashboard that has a radar for possible icy objects, a top stars list and spectrum analysis. Accounts let users save and share stars and views.

Benefits and intended impact
Space data is usually heavy and confusing. Our tool is light, fast and written in plain language, so students, teachers, researchers and space fans can explore real SPHEREx data without special software. We hope it makes the moving sky easier to understand and encourages more people to use NASA’s open data.

Tools and technologies
Python 3.13, FastAPI and Uvicorn for the server, reproject for image alignment, Bokeh for interactive spectra, HTML and JavaScript with Aladin Lite for the map, IRSA and Gaia data, and Figma for the design.

What is creative
The forecast mode with a past trail, the icy object radar, and a light, uncluttered map that avoids the dark, crowded displays of existing tools.

Factors we considered
Speed (small previews instead of large files), clarity (less clutter, simple labels), open and free data, and honesty about limits: forecasts assume steady motion, so accuracy drops over long periods.
